A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the current ACMG/AMP criteria are sufficient to classify most germline TP 53 pathogenic variants, with the exception of variants that are associated with early‐onset breast cancers.
the use of HER2+ status as a quantitative predictor of germline TP553 pathogenicity is feasible, and that the current ACMG/AMP framework for TP53 is robust enough to incorporate this information.

, in general, HER2+ status can be used as a predictor of pathogenicity for early onset breast tumors, and it is likely that this information could also be incorporated into the ACMG/AMP guideline for germline variants of other genes.

breast tumor pathology is a promising source of evidence for TP53 variant pathogenicity classification, and we hope that this work will encourage further research and the development of more comprehensive models.
